stanzas: That desirable radiance of the god Savitr may we meditate on,
who shall spur on our thoughts. (10)

notes: line 1.1: dhīmahi is disputed. Grammatically it is most often taken from dhā- 'to place, receive' ('may we receive / take to ourselves'); the traditional reading takes it from dhī- 'to think' ('may we meditate on'). Either can be printed; the editor may prefer 'may we meditate on' as the sense most readers know.

line 1.2: yo (masculine 'who') refers to Savitr, the god, not to bhargas (neuter 'radiance'). dhiyaḥ: thoughts, insights, also prayers / poetic visions. pracodayāt: 'may he impel, urge on' (optative-like subjunctive).
Savitr (Savitṛ), 'the Impeller', a solar god of the Rigveda; kept as a name. vareṇya: 'to be chosen, choice, excellent'.

The text is the bare Rigveda verse 3.62.10, without the oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ that is prefixed in recitation; romanized with the sandhi joins as written (tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ = tat savitur vareṇyaṃ). The verse number ||10|| is kept.
